extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on when and how to require restriction (election) in U.S. patent applications and how to handle double patenting issues, including special rules for Markush claims, rejoinder, provisional elections, and transitional applications. Intended to direct examiner actions and inform applicants of procedural and substantive consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'Independent' inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Independent' means not dependent, or unrelated; there is no disclosed relationship between the two or more inventions claimed (i.e., they are unconnected in design, operation, and effect).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: a process and an apparatus incapable of being used to practice the process are independent inventions. See MPEP § 806.06 and § 808.01 for related guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'Related but Distinct' inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Related inventions are those disclosed as connected in design, operation, or effect (e.g., combination and subcombination, process and product). Related inventions are 'distinct' if the inventions as claimed are not connected in at least one of design, operation, or effect and at least one invention is PATENTABLE (novel and nonobvious) OVER THE OTHER.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinctness may require a two-way test in some situations (see MPEP § 806.05(c) and § 806.05(j)). Decisions use the terms with varying meanings—read carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction is the practice of requiring an applicant to elect a single claimed invention for examination when independent inventions and/or two or more distinct inventions are claimed in an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restriction may apply to combinations/subcombinations, product/process, or species within a genus.

rubrics_metrics.name: When restriction is proper (overall criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction is proper only if claims can support separate patents and the claimed inventions are either independent or distinct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If search and examination of all claims can be made without serious burden, the examiner must examine them on the merits even if they include claims to independent or distinct inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two specific criteria for restriction between patentably distinct inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: (A) The inventions must be independent or distinct as claimed; and (B) There would be a serious search and/or examination burden on the examiner if restriction is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both criteria must be demonstrated to support a restriction requirement; see MPEP § 803.02 and § 808.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serious search/examination burden — prima facie showings
rubrics_metrics.description: A serious search burden may be prima facie shown by explanation of separate classification, separate status in the art, or a different field of search. A serious examination burden may be shown by non-prior-art issues (e.g., 35 U.S.C. 101, 35 U.S.C. 112(a)) relevant to one invention but not the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A prima facie showing of burden may be rebutted by applicant showings/evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guideline: Examiners must provide reasons/examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners must provide reasons and/or examples to support conclusions for restriction, but need not cite documents to support the restriction requirement in most cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where plural inventions are capable of being viewed as related in two ways, both applicable criteria for distinctness must be demonstrated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction should not be required if inventions are admitted obvious over each other
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is an express admission that the claimed inventions would have been obvious over each other within the meaning of 35 U.S.C. 103, restriction should not be required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited authority: In re Lee, 199 USPQ 108 (Comm’r Pat. 1978).

rubrics_metrics.name: Review/signing authority for restriction requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Only an examiner with permanent full signatory authority or temporary full signatory authority may sign final Office actions containing a final requirement for restriction; examiners with partial signatory authority may sign non-final Office actions containing a requirement for restriction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is to guard against issuance of improper restriction requirements that could lead to two patents for the same invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markush claims — when provisional election is allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: For Markush claims, the examiner may generally choose to require a provisional election of species from among patentably indistinct species or groups of species; the applicant’s election serves as a starting point for search and examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If members of a proper Markush group are few or closely related so that searching/examining entire claim is possible without serious burden, examiner must examine all members and not require provisional election. See MPEP § 808.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper Markush grouping test
rubrics_metrics.description: A Markush grouping is proper if (1) the members share a 'single structural similarity,' and (2) the members share a common use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When Markush grouping describes part of a combination/process, members must be substitutable to achieve same intended result. For chemical compounds, consider the compound as a whole (In re Harnisch). Improper Markush grouping rejections should be made on the merits (MPEP § 2117).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional election procedure for Markush claims
rubrics_metrics.description: When requiring provisional election of species, examiner will generally require election of a species or a grouping of patentably indistinct species for initial search and examination; the examiner should not require election between species that are not patentably distinct or where no serious burden exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should typically call to request telephonic election and note whether election was with or without traverse; use form paragraph 8.23 (or 8.23.01 if applicant declined telephone election).

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial examination after election — treatment when elected species rejected
rubrics_metrics.description: If the elected species (or group) is anticipated by or obvious over prior art, make the appropriate art-based rejection of any claim that reads on the elected species; non-elected species remain held withdrawn from further consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a Markush grouping was improper, make an improper Markush grouping rejection (form paragraph 8.40) in the Office action on the merits and advise species not belonging to the proper grouping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial examination after election — treatment when elected species allowable
rubrics_metrics.description: If the elected species is not anticipated/obvious, extend search and examination to non-elected species that fall within the scope of a proper Markush grouping that includes the elected species, but examiner need not extend search beyond the proper Markush grouping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continue until prior art found that anticipates/renders obvious another species in the proper grouping or determine no prior art rejection can be made. Ensure record clarity about which species have been searched and found allowable; modify/withdraw provisional election as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final rejection and finality of election requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An Office action may be made final under MPEP §§ 706.07 - 706.07(b). If a claim to a proper Markush grouping encompassing patentably distinct inventions is rejected in a proper final rejection after a provisional election, the election loses its provisional status and is given full effect under 35 U.S.C. 121.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may petition for review (37 CFR 1.144) if provisional election was made with traverse; amendments cancelling a rejected species after final may be denied entry under 37 CFR 1.116; no Markush claim can be allowed until improper grouping rejection overcome/withdrawn and all other conditions of patentability satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional application exceptions (37 CFR 1.129)
rubrics_metrics.description: For certain long-pending applications (pending at least three years as of June 8, 1995), no requirement for restriction or filing of divisionals shall be made or maintained after June 8, 1995, except where specified conditions apply (e.g., requirement first made prior to April 8, 1995; examiner did not make requirement due to applicant actions; fee not paid).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If restriction cannot be made/maintained under the paragraph, applicant will be notified and given time to elect and pay fees or file petition; see 37 CFR 1.129 for full procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejoinder of process claims upon allowance of product
rubrics_metrics.description: When claims to a product and to a process of making and/or using the product are presented, applicant may be required to elect product or process; if applicant elects product and the product claim(s) become allowable, withdrawn process claims that depend from or otherwise require all the limitations of the allowable product claim will be considered for rejoinder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All claims to a nonelected process invention must depend from or otherwise require all limitations of the allowable product claim for rejoinder to occur. Upon rejoinder, the restriction requirement between elected product and rejoined process(es) will be withdrawn. Preserve 35 U.S.C. 121 rights by not canceling nonelected claims before rejoinder occurs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims not patentably distinct in multiple applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Where claims in two or more applications filed by the same applicant or assignee are patentably indistinct, elimination of such claims from all but one application may be required absent good and sufficient reason for retention in multiple applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make complete examination in each application and enter all appropriate rejections including provisional double patenting rejections. Use form paragraph 8.29 when conflicting claims are identical or conceded patentably indistinct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability report practice has no effect on restriction practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Patentability report practice does not affect restriction practice; reasons for insisting on restriction or holding of independence/distinctness must be applied regardless of patentability report inputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 806 and § 808 for criteria of distinctness in specific contexts (combinations/subcombinations, genus/species, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Markush improper grouping rejection and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: A rejection based on an improper Markush grouping should be made in an Office action on the merits, not in a provisional election requirement; if a written provisional election is made before the first Office action on the merits, it should not include an improper Markush grouping rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a new or amended claim introduces an improper Markush grouping during prosecution, examiner may require provisional election at that time together with any appropriate rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner obligation if no serious burden exists
rubrics_metrics.description: If the search and examination of all the claims in an application can be made without serious burden, the examiner must examine them on the merits even though they include claims to independent or distinct inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This obligation applies generally, including Markush groups that are small or closely related; see MPEP § 803 and § 808.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record clarity regarding species searched and allowable
rubrics_metrics.description: In the interest of compact prosecution, the examiner should ensure the record is clear as to which species have been searched and have been found allowable over the prior art, and indicate if provisional election has been modified or withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarity of the record is critical to proper application of 35 U.S.C. 121 in later divisional applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit search/examination to proper Markush grouping
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner need not extend the search beyond a proper Markush grouping (i.e., need not search additional species that do not share the single structural similarity and common use with the elected species).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continue examination only as necessary until prior art found that affects other species within the proper grouping or until determination that no prior art rejection of any species in the grouping can be made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of withdrawing restriction requirement on 35 U.S.C. 121 shield
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the restriction requirement is withdrawn, the provisions of 35 U.S.C. 121 are no longer applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See In re Ziegler, 443 F.2d 1211 (CCPA 1971) and MPEP § 804.01 for implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephone restriction practice
rubrics_metrics.description: In most cases where a provisional election is required, the examiner should call the applicant to request a telephonic election and should note whether the election was made with or without traverse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant elects by telephone, use form paragraph 8.23 in the next Office action on the merits; include form paragraph 8.23.01 if applicant declined telephone election.

rubrics_metrics.name: When examiner should not invite an election
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner should not invite applicant to elect any group of species that would clearly be rejectable as an improper Markush grouping or under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) if presented in a separate claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not require provisional election between species that are not patentably distinct or when no serious burden exists.
